tagline.text: A month-long July festival in Bohol honoring the 1565 blood compact

location.label: Location
location.text: Tagbilaran City and Bohol's local governments (the street dancing contest is held at the Carlos P. Garcia Sports Complex in Tagbilaran)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: July (festival month; the street dancing contest is usually on the third or fourth Sunday of July)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000~3,000 (per person, one day, estimated for transport and meals; watching events is generally free)

children.text: The Sandugo Festival is Bohol's biggest annual event, honoring the blood compact sealed in 1565 between the Bohol chieftain Sikatuna and the Spanish explorer Legazpi. Throughout July, centered on Tagbilaran, it brings fairs, Bohol Day celebrations and a street dancing contest.

Sandugo means "one blood" in Visayan. The festival commemorates the blood compact in which the Bohol chieftain Datu Sikatuna and the Spanish explorer Miguel López de Legazpi mixed their blood, drank it and swore friendship in 1565. Sources differ on the date of the compact, giving either March 16 or March 25, though the Bohol tourism office gives March 16. The festival was originally held in March and has since moved to July.

The festival opens on July 1 with Tagbilaran City Charter Day and continues all month. The Bohol tourism office says Bohol Day on July 22 and the TBTK gathering of Boholanos from around the world also take place in this period. Some events run from late June into August, so it is fair to treat all of July as festival month in any year. Fairs, evening shows and local events go on all month, but the biggest spectacle is the street dancing contest.

The highlight, as Wikipedia describes it, is the street dancing contest. It is usually held on the third or fourth Sunday of July, when teams from schools, city and municipal governments, overseas Boholano groups and other provinces parade through the streets in bright costumes and compete. The dances follow choreography set to xylophones, drums and trumpets. After the contest, the blood compact reenactment follows. In 2025, the municipality of Loboc won the grand championship on July 27, and in 2026 the contest was held on July 26.

The festival changes a little every year. In 2026, the main launch took place first in Talibon in northern Bohol on July 4, and Tagbilaran City did not enter the street dancing contest in order to focus on defending its Sinulog title in Cebu City in 2027, so nine local governments took part. Before you go, we strongly recommend checking this year's schedule on the official Bohol Sandugo website and local government announcements. If you plan your Bohol trip around the festival dates, you can see not only natural sights such as the Chocolate Hills and the beaches but also how Boholanos remember and celebrate their own history up close. Programs can change from day to day, so check once more the day before.

The central ritual of the Sandugo Festival is the reenactment of the blood compact in which Sikatuna and Legazpi shared their blood. Wikipedia says the reenactment is held at the sports complex after the contest. In 2026, a historical reenactment was also staged at the opening event. The ritual itself is short, but it means much more once you know the history behind it.

This is the festival's signature spectacle, usually held on the third or fourth Sunday of July. Each team parades through the streets with set choreography, traditional costumes, and drum and xylophone music. According to Wikipedia, the route starts around noon at the City Pier, passes through the city and ends at the Carlos P. Garcia Sports Complex, but this can change from year to year.

Tagbilaran City won the grand championship in 2023 and 2024, and Loboc's Bolibongkingking Festival team won in 2025. Wikipedia lists the 2026 winner as the Catigbian team, which entered with the Katigbawan Festival. Loboc's winning piece honored Our Lady of Guadalupe, and its drumming and group dance drew praise.

July 22 is Bohol Day, and Wikipedia says the 156th celebration in 2026 is held at the Bohol Cultural Center. As a Bohol provincial government event, it includes performances and ceremonies. It may fall on a weekday, so check the date first.

During the festival, a trade and food fair sells local products and handicrafts. One travel guide says the 2026 Sandugo Agri Fair was held at Plaza Rizal on July 13~17. You can see Bohol's local food and souvenirs in one place, which makes it a nice stop for a casual look around.

A Miss Bohol Sandugo beauty pageant is held during the festival, and winners take part in the parade. TPB materials also list nightly entertainment together with the pageant. The time and place of the pageant change every year, so check local announcements.

The Philippine Tourism Promotions Board (TPB) says events such as night shows, a night market, medical missions, a tourism expo and sports tournaments are held alongside. The whole city has a festive mood, so it is pleasant to walk around at night too. Event types and timing change every year, so check the program. Splitting the day, with the contest by day and light shows in the evening, keeps it comfortable.

Many travelers visit the Blood Compact Shrine on the roadside by Tagbilaran's seafront even on days unrelated to the festival. A bronze sculpture shows the scene of the two men's oath. Even if your trip does not match the festival schedule, stopping here for a photo helps you understand the festival's background.

items.subtitle: Example for a Sunday contest day

children.text: Have breakfast at your hotel in Tagbilaran and look around the City Pier area. On big event days roads may be closed, so allow plenty of travel time.
Claim a good viewing spot before the contest starts. Wikipedia describes the contest as starting around noon at the City Pier, but this changes every year, so check the schedule on the day.
Watch the teams parade and dance. You can see group dances set to xylophones, drums and trumpets up close.
Head toward the Carlos P. Garcia Sports Complex, where the contest ends, to see the awards and the blood compact reenactment. The venue can change from year to year.
Return to the city for dinner and enjoy the night market or an evening show.
Contest days are crowded and July can bring rain, so bring a raincoat and water.
Look around the fair grounds in Tagbilaran and browse local products. The 2026 agri fair was reported to be held at Plaza Rizal.
Visit the nearby Blood Compact Shrine to see the festival's historical background.
See Baclayon Church and the Loboc River area to take in Bohol's history and nature together.
Return to the city and catch more of the festival events.
Direct flights run from Manila to Bohol–Panglao International Airport (TAG). Airlines and schedules change, so check the latest announcements.
Hotels and flights can get crowded around the Sunday of the contest. Book early once your dates are set.
Fast ferries run from Cebu City pier to Tagbilaran pier. Operators and times change, so check locally.
A ferry lets you off in the middle of Tagbilaran, so you can walk straight to event sites around the City Pier.
From the airport on Panglao Island to Tagbilaran, take a taxi or Grab. Check the fare and travel time locally.
On contest days city roads may be congested or closed, so allow plenty of time to get from the airport into the city.
Within the city you get around by tricycle, taxi and on foot. The event sites are not far apart, but in the heat a tricycle is handy for short distances.
Events held in other municipalities require separate travel by bus or van, so check the schedule.
The Sandugo Festival is held in July. It starts with the city Charter Day on July 1, passes Bohol Day on July 22, and the street dancing contest is usually on the third or fourth Sunday.
July is the rainy season in the Philippines, so showers and typhoon effects are possible. Bring a raincoat and a waterproof bag, and leave some slack in your schedule.

Staying in Tagbilaran puts you close to the event sites. Rooms fill quickly on contest days and in the middle of the festival, so book early once your dates are set. You can also stay at a beach resort on Panglao Island and come in for the day, but plan your schedule around travel time and road conditions.

At the fair booths you can taste Bohol specialties and snacks, and city restaurants and the market are close by. On street event days many stalls along the road sell snacks and drinks. The weather is hot, so drink water often and choose street food by checking hygiene.
Check this year's schedule first on the official Bohol Sandugo website or local government announcements. As in 2026, the opening event can be held somewhere other than Tagbilaran.
The street dancing contest is usually on the third or fourth Sunday of July. Book your hotel and transport early around that date.
It takes place at midday, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water, and find a shady spot.
July is the rainy season, so pack a folding umbrella or raincoat and a waterproof phone case.
Ask before getting close to participants for photos, and do not block the parade route.
Visiting the Blood Compact Shrine as well helps you understand the festival's historical background.
Venues get crowded, so keep a close watch on your belongings, phone and wallet.
The program changes every year, so recheck participating teams and venues just before your visit.
On contest days, arrive early if possible and note the restrooms, shade and emergency exit routes in advance.
Event schedules and venues change every year, and sources disagree on dates. Be sure to check Bohol provincial and Tagbilaran City announcements just before your visit.
Descriptions of the festival give different dates, and even guides for the same year disagree. Plan around the official program.
On contest days city roads may be congested or closed. Allow plenty of time to travel to the airport and pier.
July is the rainy season, so showers may fall and typhoons can change the schedule.
In crowds, beware of pickpockets and loss, and leave valuables at your hotel.
The municipalities in the contest change every year. In 2026, Tagbilaran City did not take part.
The central city of the events, with city walks and market browsing. Most event sites are within walking distance.
One of the oldest churches in Bohol and not far from the city. It is a good stop before or after the festival.
A river in Loboc, the municipality that won the 2025 street dancing grand championship. It is famous for river cruises and fits well into a day trip before or after the festival.
Bohol's signature sight, which many travelers combine with the festival in a one-day trip.
